item.title: Self-Hosted OCSP Responder & Certificate Revocation: CFSSL vs Smallstep vs EJBCA CRL
item.description: Certificate revocation is one of the most overlooked aspects of self-hosted PKI infrastructure. When a TLS certificate is compromised, expired, or issued in error, the certificate authority must provide a mechanism for clients to verify that the certificate is no longer trusted. Without proper revocation checking, compromised certificates remain valid until their natural expiration date — potentially months or years.
